findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 3, Harm 3
Raise: Not done. Case: normal use - rendering a clean canvas with installed Chrome. `--window-size=375,900` sets the browser window, whose minimum width Chrome clamps to 500 pixels, rather than establishing a 375-pixel viewport. Consequently, the load-time `innerWidth!==375` check marks a clean page as overflowing and prevents publication. Chromium's [maintainers confirm the minimum](https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/g/devtools-reviews/c/yl-2bhnESck), and its [command handler](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chromium/chromium/main/components/headless/command_handler/headless_command.js) performs screenshot sizing after loading and dumping the DOM. Establish the actual viewport before loading and measuring the canvas; the stand-in browser currently assumes the requested window width is honored.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done. Case: normal use - a canvas populates a chart or table asynchronously after load. The overflow marker is calculated only in the `load` handler, while Chrome subsequently runs the requested 2,000 milliseconds of virtual time before capture. For example, a load handler scheduling a 500-pixel-wide element after 100 milliseconds leaves the marker `ok`, although the captured phone layout overflows. The renderer then publishes every image. Chrome's [command handler](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chromium/chromium/main/components/headless/command_handler/headless_command.js) explicitly waits for the virtual-time budget after load. Measure the settled layout used for capture, and cover this delayed-content case.
